30030b50a3.description: WillJini raises first round at $3.5M valuation, without pitching a single VC. Less than 1% of Indians have a will. For the other 99%, the transfer of property, bank accounts, investments, and businesses can leave families with confusion and legal hassles. WillJini has spent 12 years trying to change that, and has now closed its first external funding round without pitching a single venture capital fund. The estate-planning startup grew from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 50 lakh in monthly revenue over three years, using money from its clients to build the business. When it finally raised capital, the investors were people who already knew WillJini: SPJIMR MBA batchmates, close friends and some of its own channel partners. The latter are mutual fund distributors who sell WillJini’s services to end clients and, in this case, chose to invest in the company as well. "They approached us. They believed in the category before the market did," says Jugal Popat, co-founder of WillJini. The round values WillJini at $3.5 million post-money. Investors who participated in the round point to the size of the opportunity as well as their familiarity with the founders. "In my career spanning almost three and a half decades, I have seen more wealth destroyed by the absence of a will or a trust. Bharat has 1.4 billion people and crores of new crorepatis popping up, but almost no one has a succession plan,” says Priyesh Sampat, a Mumbai-based wealth advisor who invested in WillJini. “WillJini is making will-making as easy as ordering food online, legal, secure and affordable. This isn't just a fintech, it's a family tech.” Sapan Gandhi, an SPJIMR batchmate and investor, says he invested in WillJini primarily for three reasons: the massive market opportunity, a problem worth solving, and having personally known both the founders. “Living in the US, I've seen how established this industry is there. 54bf028ffb.description: Thunder Compute (YC S24) | C++ Systems, Infrastructure, BizOps | San Francisco (Onsite) | Full-time | https://www.thundercompute.com We're building the VMware for GPUs. Most GPUs in the cloud sit idle a lot of the time because they're bolted to one machine over PCIe. We decouple them. Our virtualization layer is a userspace shim, loaded through LD_PRELOAD, that intercepts CUDA calls and ships them over the network to a host with a physical GPU somewhere else in the data center. Workloads run unchanged. When a process goes idle, the GPU detaches and gets reassigned, and reattaches in tens of milliseconds when it's needed again. Think Ceph for GPUs: the GPU becomes a network resource a cluster-wide scheduler can pool and pack. The hard part is making that fast. We're within ~10% of native on most AI workloads, and it lets us serve ~1.8x more users on the same fleet. We run it in production as our own GPU cloud and sell it to enterprises with underutilized fleets. Team is from Citadel Securities, Aquatic, Old Mission, AWS, and Bain. Series A, $17.5M raised from Matrix and Y Combinator. Open roles: - Software Engineer, C++ Systems ($215K-$325K + meaningful equity). Low-level, latency-sensitive work on the virtualization layer. Quant dev / HFT background preferred: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/2efae53b-817c-43e7-9... - Software Engineer, Infrastructure ($150K-$250K + meaningful equity). Go, Kubernetes, reliable systems at scale: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/927a922b-c607-4b0e-a... - Business Operations Lead ($150K-$225K + meaningful equity): https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/4f28e418-b77b-446e-a... If you're cracked at building systems software and want to do something more meaningful than creating liquidity, reach out. Email me at [redacted] and mention HN. I read every email.

5a1173b496.description: Thunder Compute (YC S24) | C++ Systems, Infrastructure, BizOps | San Francisco (Onsite) | Full-time | https://www.thundercompute.com We're building the VMware for GPUs. Most GPUs in the cloud sit idle a lot of the time because they're bolted to one machine over PCIe. We decouple them. Our virtualization layer is a userspace shim, loaded through LD_PRELOAD, that intercepts CUDA calls and ships them over the network to a host with a physical GPU somewhere else in the data center. Workloads run unchanged. When a process goes idle, the GPU detaches and gets reassigned, and reattaches in tens of milliseconds when it's needed again. Think Ceph for GPUs: the GPU becomes a network resource a cluster-wide scheduler can pool and pack. The hard part is making that fast. We're within ~10% of native on most AI workloads, and it lets us serve ~1.8x more users on the same fleet. We run it in production as our own GPU cloud and sell it to enterprises with underutilized fleets. Team is from Citadel Securities, Aquatic, Old Mission, AWS, and Bain. Series A, $17.5M raised from Matrix and Y Combinator. Open roles: - Software Engineer, C++ Systems ($215K-$325K + meaningful equity). Low-level, latency-sensitive work on the virtualization layer. Quant dev / HFT background preferred: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/2efae53b-817c-43e7-9... - Software Engineer, Infrastructure ($150K-$250K + meaningful equity). Go, Kubernetes, reliable systems at scale: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/927a922b-c607-4b0e-a... - Business Operations Lead ($150K-$225K + meaningful equity): https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/thundercompute/4f28e418-b77b-446e-a... If you're cracked at building systems software and want to do something more meaningful than creating liquidity, reach out. Email me at carl@thundercompute.com and mention HN. I read every email.

We’ve both spent our careers at the intersection of finance and technology, and we’re using that experience to rethink how markets are analyzed, tested, and traded in the age of agents. Scalar Field is built around a simple belief: over the next few years, agents will not just help people research markets — they will actively participate in them. And most platforms still assume the human is the only decision-maker. Scalar Field changes that. We’re building an agentic trading platform where users can create financial agents that research data, backtest strategies, monitor market events, and trigger trades when specific conditions are met. The long-term vision is agentic ETFs: portfolios created, managed, and rebalanced by agents around any idea, narrative, event, or market signal. Deep learning transformed text and images but mostly skipped tables, which are still the data behind most clinical trials, financial models and scientific experiments. The reason is structural: no natural sequence, no spatial structure, no shared vocabulary across datasets, so the architectures and scaling laws behind LLMs don't transfer. Our approach: pre-train a transformer on millions of synthetic datasets sampled from causal-structure priors. The whole dataset goes in as context, predictions come out in one forward pass. No per-dataset training, no hyperparameter tuning, seconds instead of hours. TabPFN v2 was published in Nature and set a new state of the art; TabPFN-3 scales to 10M rows. 4M+ downloads, 8k+ GitHub stars, in production from liquid biopsy to rail maintenance. Code: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP, with more than EUR 1B committed over four years. Models stay open, research stays public, same team and offices. Roles (most can sit in any of the three offices): - Technical Product Manager, Integrations: take every model release live across SAP (AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud), the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, and help decide which channels we build next. Reports to me, close to the code. - ML Engineer, Infrastructure: own multi-cluster GPU infra (Slurm on GCP today, multi-provider next), training performance and the tooling layer. For the other 99%, the transfer of property, bank accounts, investments, and businesses can leave families with confusion and legal hassles. WillJini has spent 12 years trying to change that, and has now closed its first external funding round without pitching a single venture capital fund. The estate-planning startup grew from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 50 lakh in monthly revenue over three years, using money from its clients to build the business. When it finally raised capital, the investors were people who already knew WillJini: SPJIMR MBA batchmates, close friends and some of its own channel partners. The latter are mutual fund distributors who sell WillJini’s services to end clients and, in this case, chose to invest in the company as well. "They approached us. They believed in the category before the market did," says Jugal Popat, co-founder of WillJini. The round values WillJini at $3.5 million post-money. Investors who participated in the round point to the size of the opportunity as well as their familiarity with the founders. "In my career spanning almost three and a half decades, I have seen more wealth destroyed by the absence of a will or a trust. Bharat has 1.4 billion people and crores of new crorepatis popping up, but almost no one has a succession plan,” says Priyesh Sampat, a Mumbai-based wealth advisor who invested in WillJini. “WillJini is making will-making as easy as ordering food online, legal, secure and affordable. This isn't just a fintech, it's a family tech.” Sapan Gandhi, an SPJIMR batchmate and investor, says he invested in WillJini primarily for three reasons: the massive market opportunity, a problem worth solving, and having personally known both the founders. “Living in the US, I've seen how established this industry is there. As per Entrackr’s estimate, the company is valued at around Rs 2,050 Cr or $215 million during the round. Founded in 2019 by Nagendra Nagaraja, Bengaluru-based QpiAI is a deeptech startup building quantum computing and AI solutions for enterprises. The company develops proprietary quantum hardware and software for applications across drug discovery, manufacturing, finance, pharma, and materials science. It has developed a 25-qubit quantum computer and is working towards a 64-qubit system, with a roadmap to scale to 1,000 qubits by 2030. QpiAI has yet to file its FY26 financials. During the fiscal year ended March 2025, it remained at a pre-revenue stage, with operating revenue of around Rs 2 Cr, while its losses increased to Rs 16.67 Cr in the same period.

We're tackling this by combining a low-latency Rust fast-fetch engine (JA4/TLS and HTTP/2 frame emulation) with an isolated stealth browser fleet, zero-code schema validation (JSON Schema/Pydantic), and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. Trade-offs / where we fit: If you just need to curl a few static Wikipedia pages, a 10-line Python script is better and cheaper. But if you need reliable, structured data out of bot-defended sites without babying headless browsers, that's what we do. We're looking for: 1. Rust Systems Engineer: High-concurrency network I/O, Axum/Tokio, TLS/BoringSSL fingerprinting, proxy routing matrices, and low-latency data pipelines. 2. Browser Security Engineer: Deep familiarity with browser internals (Firefox/Chromium source), canvas/WebGL/audio fingerprint evasion, CDP/WebDriver stealth, and familarity with anti-bot defenses. bd66c423dd.description: Team size: 3. The shared context layer for recursive companies - your work, your… Knowledge work is being restructured by AI. Strategy happens in Claude. Research happens in ChatGPT. Building happens in Claude Code and Codex. Meetings get recorded, notes get written, agents run for hours and leave behind traces nobody reads. The people defining the next decade of work are already thinking with AI every day. But none of that thinking compounds. Every session starts from zero. The reasoning behind decisions, the context behind strategies, the evolution of ideas across hundreds of conversations - all of it evaporates. Nessie is the infrastructure that makes it permanent. We auto-sync AI conversations and agent traces across every major provider - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and more - alongside meetings, notes, and email from tools like Granola, Read AI, Plaud, and Obsidian. Everything a team produces with AI flows into one place and compounds over time. Nessie turns that raw, heterogeneous data into an ontology: the live state of a company. Not a static schema but a continuously updated record of what the company knows, what it has decided, who owns what, and how its thinking has evolved, kept current as new work flows in. It is queryable from any agent through our CLI, MCP connector, and plugins, shareable across a team with real permissions, and deployable on-prem for organizations that need it. Then the loop closes. Once a company’s state is legible to its agents, every agent run becomes training signal: which skills worked, which failed, which workflows keep repeating. Nessie feeds that signal back as reviewable improvements to the skills, prompts, and processes the team runs on. This is what makes a company recursive: its agents get better from its own history, the people working with them get better too, and the compounding never stops. c5c53903dd.description: Quanfluence Raises $10 Mn To Build Full-Stack Photonic Quantum Computer. Bengaluru-based quantum compute startup Quanfluence has raised $10 Mn (around ₹92 Cr) in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing backer Pi Ventures. Quanfluence plans to deploy the fresh capital to further develop its full-stack photonic quantum computing system, bringing together indigenously designed photonic chips, control electronics and software into a single architecture. The startup is targeting early processors by 2027, followed by larger and scalable quantum machines by 2029. Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Aditi Vaidya, Anil Prabhaka, and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence is building a universal photonic quantum computer and has deployed a quantum-inspired optical Ising machine. The IIT-Madras incubated startup’s core technology includes an optical Ising machine that uses light waves as computational units. The system can process hundreds of interconnected variables simultaneously, making it 100X faster than traditional optimisation methods. Chakravarty told Inc42 that Quanfluence has already commercialised its optical Ising machine, selling the physical systems to customers as well as offering remote access to the machines on a usage-based model. The startup has sold around three machines and currently runs paid pilots with 10-15 corporations. The approach could help Quanfluence generate commercial traction while it works on the significantly harder problem of building a scalable universal quantum computer. The startup’s immediate challenge, however, is less about proving the underlying concept and more about integrating its components, scaling manufacturing and navigating long chip-production and hardware-delivery cycles. With a current team size of 25 employees, it is expecting to scale their workforce to 40-member team over the next year. Previously, Quanfluence raised $2 Mn (around ₹16.7 Cr) i

cad382de86.description: Edtech startup Arivihan raises $10 Mn in Series A led by Accel and Prosus. Bengaluru- based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in Series A funding from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures, along with an additional $200,000 from its existing GSF angel investors. The round takes the company’s total funding to more than $15 million. Entrackr recently reported on the company’s new funding and estimated that its valuation had jumped 3.3X to around $60 million. The fresh capital will be used to expand into new states and strengthen its presence in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Bihar. The company also plans to expand its CBSE offering, develop more vernacular language capabilities and increase its AI research efforts. Founded in 2022 by Ritesh Singh Chandel, Sonu Kumar and Rushabh Kothari, Arivihan offers an AI based learning platform for school students. Its platform provides interactive video lessons, instant doubt solving and AI driven study plans without relying on live teachers. The company currently serves students preparing for State Board, CBSE and NEET exams, with a focus on students from tier 2, tier 3 cities and rural areas. Arivihan said around 80% of its subscribers come from tier 3 cities and rural India. Arivihan will also scale its digital marketing and on ground distribution network as it expands across India. The company plans to hire across key functions and launch new crash courses. Arivihan was previously part of Accel’s Atoms accelerator programme and received seed funding through the programme in March 2024. The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Arivihan’s revenue jumped nearly 14.8X to Rs 3.14 crore from Rs 21.29 lakh in FY24, while the company posted a loss of Rs 4.45 crore.

Ecosystem Platform for Restaurants in India Explorex — The Memory Layer for Physical Commerce ~90% of Indian retail happens in person, yet offline venues have no memory of their customers. Restaurants run on disconnected tools, and every visit ends with zero data captured. Explorex fixes this by owning both sides of the dining transaction. Because we operate the restaurant OS and the consumer touchpoint, this data is irreplicable. We're now building Elara, an AI dining concierge that turns this data into real-time decision-making — factoring intent, context, availability, and historical behavior. This moves us beyond discovery into becoming the intelligence layer for offline commerce. Today, Explorex powers 250+ partner restaurants and 3M+ diners across Bangalore and Hyderabad, processing 8M+ transactions annually (18M+ lifetime), and operates at breakeven. Explorex is not a SaaS tool — it is the infrastructure layer for offline dining, with AI and consumer experience at its core.
